div1.head: ACT FIRST
div1.stage: The Commander enters with Flores and Ortuño, servants.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Does the Master know I have come to town?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: He does, sir.

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: The years will bring discretion.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I am Fernán Gómez de Guzmán.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: To-day youth may serve as his excuse.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: If he is ignorant of my name, let him respect the dignity of the High Commander.

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: He were ill advised to fail in courtesy.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Or he will gain little love. Courtesy is the key to favor while discourtesy is stupidity that breeds enmity.

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: Should a rude oaf hear how roundly he was hated, with the whole world at his heels not to bark but to bite, he would die sooner than convict himself a boor.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Slight no man. Among equals pride is folly but toward inferiors it becomes oppression. Here neglect is want of care. The boy has not yet learned the price of favor.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: The obligation which he assumed with the sword the day that the cross of Calatrava as fixed upon his breast, bound him to humility and love.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: He can intend no despite that his quick spirit shall not presently make appear.

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: Return, sir, nor stay upon his pleasure.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I have come to know this boy.

div1.stage: Enter the Master of Calatrava and Attendants.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: A thousand pardons, Fernán Gómez de Guzmán! I am advised of your arrival in the city.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I had just complaint of you, for my affection and our birth are holy ties, being as we are the one Master of Calatrava, and the other Commander, who subscribes himself yours wholly.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: I had no thought of this purposed honor, Fernando, hence a tardy welcome. Let me embrace you once again.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Vying in honor. I have staked my own on your behalf in countless causes, even answering during your minority before the Pope at Rome.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: You have indeed. By the holy token that we bear above our hearts, I repay your love, and honor you as I should my father.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I am well content.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: What news of the war at the front?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Attend and learn your obligation.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: Say I am already in the field.

lg.l: Through bravery of a mighty sire
As was confirmed by oaths and surety
Harkening to the voice of honor,
Of kin and allies, wisely led.
The line of her succession is not clear,
Under the protection of your cousin,
Who loves you as a brother.
Few men will gain the day.
To the hearts of those who say
Upon the sagging bosom of a child.
Flaunting the laurels of their might
Till in battle, like the cross,
Must glow and flame with red!
And with my kin bear arms.
Then shall I pass at Ciudad Real
That men may see it shine,
Livid with the passion of the cross,

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: I prayed he would never come back.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: When I brought the word I knew it would grieve you.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Would to God he had never seen Fuente Ovejuna!

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Laurencia, many a girl has made a pretense of saying no, yet all the while her heart has been as soft as butter in her.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: I am a live-oak, gnarled and twisted.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Yes, but why refuse a drink of water?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: I do, be the sun never so hot, though you may not believe it. Why love Fernando? He’s no husband.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: No, woman.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: And amen! Plenty of girls in the village have trusted the Commander to their harm.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: It will be a miracle if you escape.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: You are blind, because I have avoided him a full month now, Pascuala, and no quarter. Flores, who lays his snares, and that villain Ortuño, offered me a waist, a necklace and a head-dress. They praised Fernando, their master, and pictured him so great that I blushed at his very glory, but for all that they could not move me.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: But where was this?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Down by the brook there, a week gone yesterday.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: You’re already lost, Laurencia.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: No, no, no!

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Maybe the priest might believe your story.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: I am too innocent for the priest. In His Name, Pascuala, but of a morning rising early I had rather set me a slice of ham on the fire to munch with a crust of bread of my own kneading, filching a glass meanwhile out of the old stopped butt, once mother’s back is turned, to wet my thirst, and then climb up to watch the cow thrash through the cabbages, all foaming at the mouth come noon-day, while I hearten myself with a bit of egg-plant and a strip of bacon after hard walking, and return weary toward supper-time to nibble the raisins, home-grown in our own vineyard, which God fend the hail from, sitting me down with a dish of salad and pepper and olive oil, and so to bed tired at nightfall, in contentment and peace, with a prayer on my lips to be preserved from the men, devils, God knows, every one, than I would deliver myself up to their wiles for all their love and fury. What they want is to undo us, joy in the night and at dawning a maid’s mourning.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: You are right, Laurencia, for a sated lover flies faster than a farm sparrow. In the winter when the fields are bare they sing ‘tweet’ under the eaves till they come by the crumbs from the farmer’s board, but when the fields are green and frost has been forgotten, instead of fluttering down to sing ‘tweet’ they hop up to the roof-tree and cry ‘twit’, and ‘twit’ it is at you standing down below, make the most that you can of their twitting. Men are the same. When they need us we are their very lives, their heart, their soul, their entire being, but their hunger satisfied off they fly and leave us, too, with the echo of their twitting. So I say no man can be trusted.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: You defeat yourself, Barrildo.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Two judges are here who can decide between us.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Agree upon the forfeit and then we’ll call in the girls. If they favor me, you hand me both your shirts, with whatever else you have on your backs, in meed of victory.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Agreed. But what will you give if you lose?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: My rebeck of old box, which is worth more than a granary, for God knows its like cannot be bought in the village.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Fairly said and offered.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Done! –God save you, ladies.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Frondoso calls us ladies.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO

lg.l: The blind we say are one-eyed,
The dumb now hold their tongues,
None so active as the meddler
That large feet proclaim the faithful,
While a blotched and pimpled face-full
The lie to-day a truth is,
And if you have a hump,

sp.p: For otherwise there is no telling what names I might call you.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: In the city praise may be the fashion, Frondoso, but by my faith we have a contrary custom in the country, where words are sharp and barbed, upon tongues that are calloused to use them.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Who speaks knows.

lg.l: There is not enough to hurt you,

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Devil of a girl!

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: On my soul, she is too quick for us!

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: A pinch of spice plashed into the holy water the day of her christening.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Well, well, since you question us, let us have it without delay and judge truly.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: I’ll set out the argument.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Plant in season, then, and begin.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Attend, Laurencia.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Oh, I’ll have an answer for you some day.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Be fair, be just.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: What is this wager?

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Barrildo and I oppose Mengo.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Mengo is right. So, there!

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: A fact is certain and plain which he denies.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: I deny it because it’s a lie and they wander from the mark.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Explain.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: He maintains there is no such things as love.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Then it takes hold of one mightily.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Yes, though it be blind, for without love the world would never go on.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: I say little, not being able to read, though I could learn, but if the elements make the world and our bodies are made of the elements which war against each other unceasingly, causing anger and discord, then where is love?

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Mengo, the world is love, here and hereafter, not discord. Harmony is love. Love is a reaching out.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: A pulling in, according to nature, which governs all things through the resemblances that are. Love is a looking to its own, it’s preservation. I raise my hand to my face to prevent the blow, I move my feet to remove me from danger to my body, my eyelids close to shield my sight through the attraction of a mutual love.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: He admits it’s love, so what then? There’s an end.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: We love ourselves, no one else, that’s flat.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Mengo, what a lie! And God forgive me. The love a man bears for a woman, or a beast for its mate, is a fierce, consuming passion.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Self-love, interest, not pure love. What is love?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: A running after beauty.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: But why run after beauty?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: For the thrill and the pleasure, boy.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: True. And the pleasure a man seeks for himself.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: True again.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: So that self-love seeks its own delight?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Granted.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Therefore there is no love, only we like what we like, and we intend in all things to get it, to seek delight, our delight.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: One day the priest preached in the village about a man named Plato who had taught men how to love, but what Plato loved, he said, was the soul and the virtue that was hidden in it.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: So the fathers teach the children in ‘cademies and schools.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Yes, and don’t you listen to any nonsense, either. Mengo, thank God you never knew the curse of love.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Were you ever in love?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: In love with my honor, always.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Come, come, ladies! Decide, decide.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Who wins?

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Let the priest or the sacristan cook up a reply, for Laurencia loves too much and I not a little, so how can we, siding both ways, decide?

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: They laugh at us.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: God guard the fair!

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: This man is from the Commander.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Why so brash, old goshawk, in the village?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: You meet me as a soldier.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: From Don Fernando?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: The war is done, though it has cost us blood, and armies of our friends.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Say what of note our brand achieved.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: I will, and that better than another, having seen it with my own eyes.

lg.l: Those who profess it on their breasts
Though robed and habited for prayer,
But now in panoply of white
Black of mane, the tail coal black,
A Turkish coat of mail he wore,
The Master is feared and praised
By deeds, by valor and by victory
Of the rape of this fair city,

sp.p: Now hear the music sound, for zest in victory adds sweetest savor.

div1.stage: The Commander enters with Ortuño and Musicians, accompanied by Juan Rojo, Regidor, Esteban and Alonso, Alcaldes.

lg.l: Acknowledgment and thanks in this our town
Receive in token of the love you show.
Accept this rustic tribute to renown,
Proffered how simply. These poor meadows grow
To Fuente Ovejuna, whose elders glow
With pride, offering homely gifts, yet apt
To please, as pod or sprout or root, in carts
Heaped high with ruddy fruits, the produce rept
From field and orchard, ripening in our hearts,
Mellowed in crib and barnyard. First, car one
Twin hampers bears of jars, baked for these marts,
Whereto are added geese that sleekly run
Long necks from tangling nets, and shrilly shrick
Cackles of praise, paeans of booty won.
Ten salted hogs bid the next wagon creak,
Bulging with fatty trimmings and dried meat;
The skins like amber shine, side, haunch and breek.
A hundred pair of capon follow, treat
For the belly, plump hens torn from the cock
Through all the eager farms, tender and meet
For axing. Arms we lack, nor bring we stock
Of blooded steeds, nor harness for the bold,
For such in rustic hands were cheat and mock
Of love’s pure gold which in our hearts is told.
Twelve wine-skins next appear, with beady wine
Filled full, in winter enemy of cold
And friendly to the soldier, ally in line
Of battle, or on defense trusty like steel,
Tempering courage, for temper springs of wine.
Unnumbered cheeses, last, jounce past awheel,
With products of the churn and dairy days,
True tokens of the love the people feel
Toward you and yours, harvests of heart-felt praise.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Thanks and be gone, Alcaldes of this town. Be gone assured of favor.

sp.speaker: ALONSO
sp.p: Rest, Master, in enjoyment of our love. These cat-tails before the door and this coarse sedge grass should bear pearls to match your deserving, as indeed we pray, and yet fall short of the devotion of the village.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I accept the gifts right gladly. So get you gone.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: The singers will repeat the refrain.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: The girls stay behind.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: No, Your Excellency.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: By the Lord you do! No airs nor graces! These are soldiers here.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Pascuala, he looks your way.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Do you teach me to be modest?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I look your way, little chuck with the crook, and tend to this burr of the pasture, till she open to me.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: We grew here, Master.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Pass into the house where my men will keep you safe.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: If the Alcaldes go in so will we, because one is my father, but a girl by herself is just a girl and must be careful.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: A word, Flores.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Master?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: How? What mean these green-briers?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Walk straight in, girls. Come!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: You let go!

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Any fool can walk.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: You’ll lock the door if we do go in.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Pass and taste the spoils of war. Come!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Aside to Ortuño Throw the bolt, Ortuño, once they’re inside.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: You hurt us, Flores.

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: These cheeses came in no cart.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: No, and we are not for you, either, so get out!

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: What can you do with a girl?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Your master has his fill to-day for one stomach.

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: He’s a judge of meat and prefers you, though the carts pass.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Then let him burst!

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: What will the Master say with never a sight of a woman for good cheer? They laugh at us.

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: Blows reward service, mostly given for villainy, so there’s no cure. It’s desert.

div1.stage: Enter the King Don Ferdinand of Aragon and Queen Isabella, accompanied by Don Manrique and Attendants.

sp.speaker: ISABELLA
sp.p: To prepare is wise. Sire, harry Alonso of Portugal where he has pitched his tents, for a ready offense averts the threatened injury.

sp.speaker: THE KING
sp.p: Navarre and Aragon dispatch swift aid and succor. Under my command the Castilian bands shall be reformed. Success lies in prevention.

sp.speaker: ISABELLA
sp.p: Majesty, prevail by strategy.

sp.speaker: DON MANRIQUE
sp.p: Two Regidors of Ciudad Real crave audience.

sp.speaker: THE KING
sp.p: Admit them to our presence.

div1.stage: Enter Two Regidors of Ciudad Real.

lg.l: Great Ferdinand the Catholic our King,
Posting from Aragon to high Castile
On warlike service and the common weal,
Humble petition to thy sword we bring
For vengeance, urging here the patent royal
Bestowed on Ciudad Real, thy city,
Foully wronged. To be thy city was our joy,
Thy will our law, proclaimed in kingly charter;
But blows of fate laid low our fealty.
A froward youth. Rodrigo Téllez Girón,
Master of Calatrava, with naked sword
Carves out addition to his wide domain,
Wasting our homes, our lands and revenues.
We met his treacherous assault, and force
Opposed to force, by threat and fear undaunted,
Till blood in rivers ran adown our streets,
Alas but vainly! The day we lost, and he,
Pricked on by the Commander Fernán Gómez,
Cunning in council, governs the city,
While we, enslaved, lament our injuries.

sp.speaker: THE KING
sp.p: Where dwells this Fernán Gómez?

lg.l: Sire, Fuente Ovejuna is his seat,
Wherein he rules amid his seignories.
He governs there does he his will,
Raining down blows upon his abject thralls
None lives. Not one, alas, of noble blood
This cause demands an instant remedy.
The walls may be surrendered to the foe,
Who thus will boldly dominate the pass,
And with two chosen companies chastise
This arrogance, denying let or stay.
The Count of Cabra shall by our command
As swiftly follow, bravest of the house
The front of tyranny must bow
In the presence of our majesty.

div1.stage: A river bank near Fuente Ovejuna.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: I had not wrung the sheets, you saucy Frondoso, when you drove me from the river bank with spying. While we gaze the country-side talks and waits on tip-toe. The sturdiest of our ladies, your jacket is the gayest and the costliest, so others note what you do, and not a girl in the village nor herdsman on the hills nor down in the river bottoms but swears we are one and of right ought to be joined, while Juan Chamorro, the sacristan, leaves his piping to publish the banns, for love, they say, goes first to church. Ah, wine burst the vaults in August, and burst every pot with must but I heed them not nor attend to their chatter, though it be time, methinks, and time soon for our own good to put an end to all this idle talk and pother.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Laughing Laurencia, I die while you smile. Though I say nothing you will not hear me, till at last I have scarcely strength even to mutter. I would be your husband but you repay with taunts my faith and loyalty.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: I encourage you all I can.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: It’s not enough. When I think of you I cannot eat, drink or sleep. I starve yet love an angel. God knows I die.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Cross yourself, Frondoso, or else bethink you of some charm.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: There’s a charm for two doves at the church, love, that makes them one. God set us beak to beak!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Speak to your master, Juan Rojo, if you will, and can summon the courage, else I must, since he is my uncle. Pray for the day, and hope.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Look! The Commander!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Stalking deer. Hide in the bushes.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Big bucks are hard to hide.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Aha! Following the fawn, I hit upon the doe.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: I was resting from washing and return to the brookside now, Commander.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Sweet Laurencia, stay, nor obscure the beauty heaven has granted to my sight. If you have escaped my hand till now, the woods and the fields will befriend us, for they are accomplices of love. Bend your pride and let your cheek flush as it has never done yet in the village. Sebastiana, who was Pedro Redondo’s wife, has been mine, and so has the chit who wedded Martín del Pozo. I came upon her two nights a bride, and she opened to me fondly.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: My Lord, they had opened to so many that their fondness was no longer in question. Ask the village. God grant you luck with the deer. The cross on your breast proclaims you are no tempter of women.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: You protest too much, lass. I put down my cross-bow. With my hands I will subdue these pretty wiles.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: No, no! What would you? Let go!

div1.stage: Frondoso re-enters and seizes the cross-bow.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Struggle is useless.

p.seg: I take the bow. Heaven grant I do not shoot.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Yield! Have done!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Heaven help me now!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: We are alone, no one will hear –

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Noble Commander, loose that girl, or your breast shall be my mark, though the cross shine clear upon it.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: The dog insults me!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Here is no dog. Laurencia, flee!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Frondoso, you take care.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Go!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Only a fool deprives himself of his sword, which I, god or devil, put by, fearing to fright the chase!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: By God above, Commander, if I loose this string I’ll gyve you like a hawk!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Betrayed! Traitorous hind, deliver up that cross-bow. Dog, set down!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: To be shot through? Hardly. Love is a warrior that yields his throne to none.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Shall a knight valiant in battle be foiled by a dumb peasant? Stay, wretch! On guard! –for I forget my rank and station.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: I do not. I am a swain, but since I will to live, I take the cross-bow with me.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Ignominy, shame! I will have vengeance to the hilt. Quickly I vanish.

div1.head: ACT SECOND

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Better touch the reserve no further. The year bodes ill with threat of foul weather, so let the grain be impounded though there be mutiny among the people.

sp.speaker: REGIDOR
sp.p: I am of your mind if the village may be governed in peace.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Then speak to Fernán Gómez. These astrologers with their harangues pretend they know secrets God only knows. Not a scrap can they read of the future, unholy fabricators of what was and what shall be, when to their eyes even the present is blank – for their ignorance is rank. Can they bring the clouds indoors and lay the stars upon the table? How do they peer into heaven and yet come down with such dire disasters? These fellows tell us how and when to sow, here with the grain, there with the barley and the vegetables, the squash, mustard, and cucumber – as squashes add them to the number. Next they predict a man will die and one does in Transylvania, or the vineyards shall suffer drought, or people take to beer in far-off Germany; also cherries will freeze and impoverish the neighbors in Gascony, while there will be a plague of tigers in Hyrcania. So or not so, pray remember – the year ends with December.

div1.stage: Leonelo, a student, enters with Barrildo.

sp.speaker: LEONELO
sp.p: I grant this town nothing, upon a re-view, but as the plain seat of stupidity.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: How did you fare in Salamanca?

sp.speaker: LEONELO
sp.p: That is no simple story.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: By this you must be a complete Bártulo.

sp.speaker: LEONELO
sp.p: Not even a barber by this. In our faculty few trim knowledge from the course.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: You return to us a scholar.

sp.speaker: LEONELO
sp.p: No, but I have learned what it is wise to know.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: With all the printing of books nowadays a man might pick up a few and be wise.

sp.speaker: LEONELO
sp.p: We know less than we did when there was less knowledge, for the bulk of learning is so great no man can compass it. Confusion results from excess, all the stir goes to froth, while those who read befuddle their heads with endless pages and become literal slaves. The art of printing has raised up a thousand geniuses over night. To be secure it spreads and conserves the Holy Scriptures, that they may be known of all and endure, but this invention of Guttenberg, that famous German of Mayence, has in fact devitalized glory. Many a man of repute has proved a very fool when his books have been printed, or else suffered the mortification of having simpletons issue theirs in his name. Others have set down arrant nonsense and credited it to their enemies out of spite, to whose undoing it circulates and appalls the world.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: I can find no words to argue with you.

sp.speaker: LEONELO
sp.p: The ignorant have the learned at their mercy.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Leonelo, on every account printing is a mighty invention.

sp.speaker: LEONELO
sp.p: For centuries the world did very well without it, and to this hour it has not produced one Jerome nor a second Augustine. The men were saints.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Sit down and rest, for my head is dizzy opposing you.

div1.stage: Juan Rojo and a Farmer enter.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: There is not a dower on four of these farms if the fields continue as they are, and this may be seen on all sides, far and near, for all is one.

sp.speaker: FARMER
sp.p: What word of the Commander?

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Would Laurencia had never set foot by the river!

sp.speaker: FARMER
sp.p: I could dangle him gladly from that olive-tree, savage, unbridled and lewd!

div1.stage: The Commander enters with Ortuño and Flores.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Heaven for the just!

sp.speaker: REGIDOR
sp.p: Commander!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: God’s body, why do you stand?

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Señor, where the custom is to sit, we stand.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I tell you to sit down.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: As honorable men we cannot do you honor, having none.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Sit down while I talk with you!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Shall we discuss my hound, sir?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Alcalde, these true men of mine praise the rare virtue of the animal.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: The beast is swift. In God’s name but he can overtake a thief or harry a coward right cruelly.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I would set him on a graceful hare that these days lopes before me.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Done, if you will lead us to the hare.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Oh, speaking of your daughter –

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: My daughter?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Yes, why not? The hare.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: My daughter is not your quarry.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Alcalde, pray you prevail upon her.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: How?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: She plumes herself before me. A wife, and a proud one, of a councilor who attends before me now, and listens, at my every look darts kindling glances.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: She does ill. You, Señor, do ill also, speaking thus freely.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Oh, what rustic virtue! Here, Flores, get him the book of Politics , and let him perfect himself in Aristotle.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Señor, the town would live in the reflection of your honor. There be men in Fuente Ovejuna.

sp.speaker: LEONELO
sp.p: I never read of such a tyrant.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: What have I said, in faith, to which you take exception, Regidor?

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: You have spoken ill. Speak well, for it is not meet you level at our honor.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Your honor? Good! Are we importing friars to Calatrava?

sp.speaker: REGIDOR
sp.p: There be those that be content to wear the cross, though the heart be not too pure.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I do not injure you, mingling my blood with yours.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: A smirch is no hidden stain.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: In doing my will I accord your wives honor.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: The very words spell dishonor, while your deeds pass all remedy.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Obstinate dolt! Ah, better the cities where men of parts and renown wreak their will and their pleasure! There husbands give thanks when their wives sacrifice upon the altar.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: They do no such service, if with this you would move us. God rules, too, in the cities, and justice is swift.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Get up and get out.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: We have said what you have heard.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Out of the square straight! Let not one remain behind!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: We firmly take our leave.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: What? In company?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: By the rood, hold your hand!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: These hinds would slander me, defiling the square with lies, departing together.

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: Pray be patient.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I marvel that I am so calm! Walk each one by himself, apart. Let no man speak till his door has shut behind him!

sp.speaker: LEONELO
sp.p: Great God, can they stomach this?

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: My path lies this way.

div1.stage: Esteban, Juan Rojo, Regidor, Leonelo and the Peasants go out, leaving the Commander, Flores and Ortuño.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: What shall we do with these knaves?

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: Their speech offends you and you by no means hide your unwillingness to hear it.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Do they compare themselves with me?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Perversity of man.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Shall that peasant retain my cross-bow and not be punished while I live?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Last night we took him, as we thought, at Laurencia’s door, and I gave an oaf who was his double a slash that married his two ears.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Can you find no trace of that Frondoso?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: They say he remains in these parts still.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: And dares remain, who has attempted my life?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Like a silly bird or a fish, a decoy will tempt him and he will fall into the lure.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: That a laborer, a stripling of the soil should aim a cross-bow at a captain before whose sword Córdoba and Granada tremble! Flores, the end of the world has come!

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Blame love, for it knows no monopoly of daring.

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: Seeing he lived, I took it as a token of your kindly disposition.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Ortuño, the smile is false. Dirk in hand, within these two hours would I ransack the place, but vengeance yields the rein to reason until the hour shall come. Which of you had a smile of Pascuala?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: She says she intends to marry.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: How far is she prepared to go?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: She will advise you anon when she can accept a favor.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: How of Olalla?

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: Fair words.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Buxom and spirited! How far?

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: She says her husband has been uneasy these past days, suspicious of my messages, and of your hovering about, attended. As soon as his fears are allayed, you shall have a sign.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: On the honor of a knight ‘tis well! These rustics have sharp eyes and commonly are evil-minded.

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: Evil-minded, ill-spoken and ill-favored.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Say not so of Inés.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Which one?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Antón’s wife. Aha!

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Yes, she will oblige any day. I saw her in the corral, which you can enter secretly.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: These easy girls we requite but poorly. Flores, may women never learn the worth of the wares they sell!

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: No pain wipes out the sweetness wholly. To prevail quickly, cheats the expectation, but, as philosophers agree, women desire the men as they are desired, nor can form be without substance, at which we should not complain, nor wonder.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: A man who is fiercely swept by love finds solace in a speedy yielding to desire, but afterward despises the object, for the road to forgetfulness even under the star of honor, is to hold oneself cheap before love’s importuning.

sp.speaker: CIMBRANOS
sp.p: Where is the Commander?

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: Behold him, if you have the faculty of sight.

lg.l: By title of the Castilian Queen,
Lay siege to Don Rodrigo Girón
Forfeiting the spoils so dearly won
At cost of blood of Calatrava.
Quartered with the bars of Aragon.
What though the King of Portugal
Vanquished, the Master must creep home

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: That shall never be.

div1.stage: Mengo enters with Laurencia and Pascuala, running.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Don’t leave us.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: What’s the matter?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Mengo, we seek the village in groups, when there’s no man to go with us, for fear of the Commander.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: How can the ugly devil torment so many?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: He is upon us night and day.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Oh, would heaven send a bolt to strike him where he stands!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: He’s an unchained beast, poison, arsenic and pestilence throughout the land.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Laurencia, they say Frondoso pointed an arrow at his breast for your sake, here in this very meadow.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Mengo, I hated all men till then, but since that day I relent. Frondoso had courage; it will cost him his life.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: He must fly these fields, that’s sure.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: I love him enough to advise it, but he’ll have no counsel of me, storming and raging and turning away. The Commander swears he will hang him feet upward.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: I say hang the Commander.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Stone him I say. God knows but I will up and at him with a rock I saved at the sheep-fold that will land him a crack that will crush his skull in! He’s wickeder than Gabalus that old Roman.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: The one that was so wicked was Heliogabalus. He was a man.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Whoever he was, call him Gab or Gal, his scurvy memory yields to this. You know history. Was there ever a man like Fernán Gómez?

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: No, he’s no man. There must be tigers in him.

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: Help in God’s name, if you are women!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Why, what’s this, Jacinta?

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: We are all your friends.

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: The Commander’s men, on their way to Ciudad Real, armed with villainy when it should be steel, would seize me and take me to him.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: God help you, Jacinta! With you, pray he be merciful, but I choose rather to die than be taken!

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Jacinta, being no man I cannot save you.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: I can because I am a man in strength and in name. Jacinta, stand beside me.

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: Are you armed?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Twice, I have two arms.

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: You will need more.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Jacinta, the ground bears stones.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Did you think you could run away from us?

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: Mengo, I am dead with fear!

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Friends, these are poor peasant girls.

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: Do you assume to defend her?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: I do, so please you, since I am her relative and must protect her, if that may be.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Kill him straightway!

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Strike me heaven, but I am in a rage! You can put a cord around my neck but, by God, I’ll sell my life dear!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Who calls? What says this turd?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: The people of this town, which we should raze for there is no health in it, insult our arms.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Señor, if pity can prevail in the face of injustice, reprove these soldiers who would force this peasant girl in your name, though spouse and parents be bred to honor, and grant me license straight to lead her home unharmed.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I will grant them license straight to harm you for your impudence. Let go that sling.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Señor –

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Flores, Ortuño and Cimbranos, it will serve to tie his hands.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Is this the voice of honor?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: What do these sheep of Fuente Ovejuna think of me?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Señor, have I offended you, or mayhap the village, in anything?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Shall we kill him?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: It would soil your arms which we shall stain with redder blood.

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: We wait your orders, sir.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Flog him without mercy. Tie him to that oak-tree, baring his back, and with the reins –

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: No, no, for you are noble!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Flog him till the rivets start from the straps!

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: My God, can such things be?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Pretty peasant, draw near daintily. Who would prefer a farmer to a valiant nobleman?

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: But will you heal my honor, taking me for yourself?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Truly I do take you.

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: No, I have an honorable father, sir, who may not equal you in birth, but in virtue he is the first.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: These are troubled days nor will this rude peasantry salve my outraged spirit. Pass with me under the trees.

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: I?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: This way.

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: Look what you do!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Refuse and I spurn you. You shall be the slut of the army.

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: No power of lust can overcome me.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Silence and go before.

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: Pity, Señor!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Pity have I none.

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: I appeal from your wickedness to God!

div1.stage: Exit the Commander, haling her out.

lg.l: To the love that I bear.
O’er the brow of the hill
And I, the slave of beauty,
And may he live a thousand years,
I’ll pray for his soul also
Yet by the book we are twain.
Say for me to the town
For this new miracle of mercy.
Oh may we marry, oh Frondoso,

div1.stage: Enter Esteban and Juan Rojo, Regidor.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: His departure outraged the square, and indeed it was most unseemly behavior. Such tyranny stuns as a blow; even poor Jacinta must pay the price of his madness.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Spain turns already to the Catholic Kings, a name by which our rulers have come to be known, and the nation renders obedience to their laws. They have appointed the Master of Santiago Captain General of Ciudad Real, dispatching him forthwith against Girón’s oppression of the town. But my heart aches for Jacinta, being as she is an honest girl.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: They beat Mengo soundly.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: I never saw dye, black or red, to rival his flesh.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Peace and no more, for my blood boils, or else congeals at his name. Have I authority or a staff of office?

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: The man cannot control his servants.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: On top of all this they chanced on Pedro Redondo’s wife one day in the very bottom of the valley, and after he insulted her she was turned over to the men.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Who is listening concealed?

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: I, a petitioner.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Granted, Frondoso. Your father brought you to be, but I have brought you to be what you are, a prop and support, who is my very son in the house.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Assured, Alcalde, of permission, I speak as one by birth honorable, and not obscure.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: You have suffered wrong at the hand of Fernán Gómez?

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: More than a little.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: My heart records it. The man is surely mad.

lg.l: Pardon presumption though it be extreme;
Boldly I speak for men shall count me bold.
Now heaven be praised, my son,
For your proposal seals our honor,

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: I have taken an oath to bestow some right good maravedis upon a good young man.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: I seek no dower. Gold, they say, makes the day dull.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: So long as he does not court the wine-skins, you may dower him without stint or mercy.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: I will speak to my daughter that assurance may be doubly sure.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Do, pray, for violence has no part in love.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Dearest daughter Laurencia!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Oh, father?

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: She approves for she answers before I speak! –Dearest daughter Laurencia, step apart a moment. Frondoso, who is an honest lad, if one there be in Fuente Ovejuna, inquires of me as to your friend Gila, whom he would honor as a wife.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Gila a wife?

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Is she a fitting mate, a proper wife?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Yes, father, oh she is! Of course!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Of course she is ugly, as ugly as they come, which led me to suggest, Laurencia, that Frondoso look at you.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Father, be serious as becomes your office.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Do you love him?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: I have favored him and am myself favored. But you knew!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Shall I say yes?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Yes, father, for me.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: The yes will do for us both. Come, we will seek his father.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Instantly.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: My boy, to return to the dower. I can afford, yes, and I pledge, four thousand maravedis.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Señor, I am your son now and you offend me.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: A day and pride abates, lad, but if you marry without a dower, by my faith, many a day will succeed and the abatement not be mended.

lg.l: I look at you and laugh,
I drink in at a glance

div1.stage: The Master, the Commander, Flores and Ortuño enter.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Fly, sir! There is no remedy.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: The wall giving way, the weight of the enemy undoes us.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: We have bled them and cost them many lives.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: The banner of Calatrava shall not trail among their spoils, though it were recompense turning all to glory.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Our league, Girón, crumbles and lies lifeless.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: Can we outstrip fortune, though she be blind, favoring us to-day, to-day to leave us?

sp.speaker: VOICES
sp.p: Within Hail, Victory! Hail, the Crown of Castile!

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: The pennons show upon the battlements while all the windows of the towers thrust banners forth, proclaiming the victory.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Much joy may they have of the day! By my soul, a day of slaughter!

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: Fernán Gómez, I’ll to Calatrava.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: And I to Fuente Ovejuna. Stay upon your cousin of Portugal, or, weighing adversity, yield allegiance to the Catholic King.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: I shall apprise you with despatch.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Time is a hard general.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: God grant me few years like this, fertile in undeception.

div1.stage: Enter the wedding-train, Musicians, Mengo, Frondoso, Laurencia, Pascuala, Barrildo, Esteban and Juan Rojo.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: A clever boy thought that up! Oh, that boy is clever!

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: He could troll it out at any wedding.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Mengo sings only to the lash because he says it has more tang to it.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Yes, and I know a young chap in the valley, not meaning you of course, who would make a nice dish for the Commander.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Enough of gloom and amen, seeing that a ferocious barbarian offers at our honor.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: I believe a hundred soldiers whipped me that day, and all I had was a sling that I gave up to protect me. However, I know a man, not mentioning names, who was full of honor and pursued with a syringe loaded with dye and some herbs that caused him great pain, and oh my, the pain that they caused him! How that man did suffer!

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: By way of jest. It was done as a laughing matter.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: As it came out afterwards. At the time he never laughed nor even suspected, but felt much better without the dye, though while it was in, death was preferable.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: A song would be preferable, or anything. Come, let it be a good one, Mengo.

l.emph: Pray God neither one of them
Just too tired out to live,
They have forgotten all about it –

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: God help the poet who made that up!

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: He needs more help.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Oh, that reminds me! Did you ever see a baker baking buns? He dips the dough into the oil until the pot is full, and then some swell up, some come out askew and twisted, leaning to the right, tumbling to the left, some scorched, some burned, some uneatable. Well, a poet’s subject is his dough, he plops a verse onto the paper hoping it will turn out sweet, and his friends all tell him so, but when he tries to sell it he has to eat himself, for the world is too wise to buy or else hasn’t the money.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: You came to the wedding so as not to give the bride and groom a chance to talk.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Uncle, you must be kissed. And you, too, Father –

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Not on the hand. May your father’s hand be your protection, and Frondoso’s also, in the hour of need.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Rojo, heaven protect her and her husband on whom I invoke an everlasting benison.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Ever to share with you.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Come all now, play and sing, for they are as good as one.

l.emph: Waits the maid with the flowing hair

div1.stage: The Commander, Flores, Ortuño and Cimbranos enter.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Let all in the house stand still on pain of death.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Señor, though this be no play, your command shall be obeyed. Will you sit down? Why all these arms and weapons? We question not, for you bring home victory.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: I am dead unless heaven helps me.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Stand behind me, Frondoso.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: No, seize and bind him.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Surrender, boy, ‘tis best.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Do you want them to kill me?

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Why, pray?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I am no man to take life unjustly, for, if I were, my soldiers would have run him through ere this, forwards or rearwards. Throw him into prison where his own father shall pronounce sentence upon him, chained in his dank cell.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: This is a wedding, Señor.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: What care I for weddings? Is this your occupation in the village?

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Pardon him, Señor, if he has done wrong, being who you are.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Pascuala, he has done no wrong to me, but offense to the Master, Téllez Girón, whom God preserve. He has mocked his law, scoffed at his rule, and punishment must be imposed as a most dire example, or there will be those to rise against the Master, seeing that one afternoon, but shortly gone, flower of these loyal and faithful vassals, he dared take aim, pointing the cross-bow at the bosom of the High Commander.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: If a father-in-law may offer a word of excuse, his dudgeon was not strange but manly, taking umbrage as a lover. You would deprive him of his wife. Small wonder the man should defend her!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Alcalde, the truth is not in you.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Be just, Señor.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I had no thought to deprive him of his wife, nor could so have done, he having none.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: But you had the thought, which shall suffice. Henceforth enough! A King and Queen rule now in Castile whose firm decrees shall bring this rioting to cease, nor will they stay their hands, these wars once ended, nor suffer arrogance to overpower their towns and villages, crucifying the people cruelly. Upon his breast the King will place a cross, and on that royal breast it shall be the symbol, too, of honor!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Death to presumption! Wrest the staff from him.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Señor, I yield it up, commanded.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Beat him with it while he capers about this stable. Have at him smartly!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Still we suffer your authority. I am ready. Begin!

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: They beat an old man?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Yes, because he is my father. Beat him, avenging yourself on me!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Arrest her, and let ten soldiers guard this sinful maid!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Justice, descend this day from Heaven!

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: No wedding but a shambles.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: And not a man of us said a word!

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: I have had my beating already and you can still see purple enough on me to outfit a Cardinal, without the trouble of sending to Rome. Try, if you don’t believe it, what a thorough job they can do.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: We must all take counsel.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: My counsel, friends, is to take nothing but forget it. I know which side I am on, though I don’t say, for it’s scaled like a salmon. Never again will any man get me to take it! Nor woman either.

div1.head: ACT THIRD
div1.stage: A room in the Town Hall at Fuente Ovejuna.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Is the Town Board assembled?

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Not a person can be seen.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Bravely we face danger!

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: All the farms had warning.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Frondoso is a prisoner in the tower and my daughter Laurencia in such plight that she is lost save for the direct interposition of heaven.

div1.stage: Juan Rojo enters with the Second Regidor.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Who complains aloud when silence is salvation? Peace, in God’s name, peace!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: I will shout to the clouds till they re-echo my complaints while men marvel at my silence.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: We came to attend the meeting.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Farmers of this village, an old man whose grey beard is bathed in tears, inquires what rites, what obsequies we poor peasants, assembled here, shall prepare for our ravished homes, bereft of honor? And if life be honor, how shall we fare since there breathes not one among us whom this savage has not offended? Speak! Who but has been wounded deeply, poisoned in respect? Lament now, yes, cry out! Well? If all be ill, how then say well? Well, there is work for men to do.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: The direst that can be. Since by report it is published that Castile is subject now to a King, who shall presently make his entrance into Córdoba, let us dispatch two Regidors to that city to cast themselves at his feet and demand remedy.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: King Ferdinand is occupied with the overthrow of his enemies, who are not few, so that his commitments are warlike entirely. It were best to seek other succor.

sp.speaker: REGIDOR
sp.p: If my voice have any weight, I declare the independence of the village.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: How can that be?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: On my soul, my back tells me the Town Board will be informed as to that directly.

sp.speaker: REGIDOR
sp.p: The tree of our patience has been cut down, the ship of our joy rides storm-tossed, emptied of its treasure. They have rapt the daughter from one who is Alcalde of this town in which we dwell, breaking his staff over his aged head. Could a slave be scorned more basely?

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: What would you have the people do?

sp.speaker: REGIDOR
sp.p: Die or rain death on tyrants! We are many while they are few.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Lift our hands against our Lord and Master?

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Only the King is our master, save for God, never these devouring beasts. If God be with us, what have we to fear?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Gentlemen, I advise caution in the beginning and ever after. Although I represent only the very simplest laborers, who bear the most, believe me we find the bearing most unpleasant.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: If our wrongs are so great, we lose nothing with our lives. An end, then! Our homes and vineyards burn. Vengeance on the tyrants!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Open, for I have need of the support of men! Deeds, or I cry out to heaven! Do you know me?

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Martyr of God, my daughter?

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: This is Laurencia.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Yes, and so changed that, gazing, you doubt still!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: My daughter!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: No, no more! Not yours.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Why, light of my eyes, why, pride of the valley?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: As well might the noble pay for the jewel lost in the merchant’s hand!

lg.l: I was lost to Fernán Gómez,

sp.p: My face is bruised and bloody in this court of honest men. Some of you are fathers, some have daughters. Do your hearts sink within you, supine and cowardly crew? You are sheep, sheep! Oh, well-named, Village of Fuente Ovejuna, the Sheep Well! Sheep, sheep, sheep! Give me iron, for senseless stones can wield none, nor images, nor pillars –jasper though they be –nor dumb living things that lack the tiger’s heart that follows him who steals its young, rending the hunter limb from limb upon the very margin of the raging sea, seeking the pity of the angry waves.

lg.l: With the cock upon their train!
Tuck your knitting in you belts,
Heave stones and do not blench.
Be heirs, boys, to our ribbons,

sp.p: For now the Commander will hang Frondoso from a merlon of the tower, without let or trial, as presently he will string you all, you race of half-men, for the women will leave this village, nor one remain behind! To-day the age of amazons returns, we lift our arms and strike against this villainy, and the crash of our blows shall amaze the world!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Daughter, I am no man to bear names calmly, opprobrious and vile. I will go and beard this despot, though the united spheres resolve against me.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: So will I, for all his pride and knavery.

sp.speaker: REGIDOR
sp.p: Let him be surrounded and cut off.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Hang a cloth from a pike as our banner and cry “Death to Monsters!”

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: What course shall we choose?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: To be at them, of course. Raise an uproar and with it the village, for every man will take an oath and be with you that to the last traitor the oppressors shall die.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Seize swords and spears, cross-bows, pikes and clubs.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Long live the King and Queen!

sp.speaker: ALL
sp.p: Live our lords and masters!

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Death to cruel tyrants!

sp.speaker: ALL
sp.p: To cruel tyrants, death!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: March on, and heaven march before you! At the door. Hello! Ho, women of this town! Draw near! Draw near for the salvation of your honor!

div1.stage: Pascuala, Jacinta and various Women enter.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Who calls us? Where are the men to-day?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Behold them down that street, marching to murder Fernán Gómez. Yes, old men, young men, and troops of eager boys, like furies run to meet him! Shall they share all the glory of this mighty day, when we women can boast wrongs that match and outstrip theirs?

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: What can we do?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Fall in behind me and we will do a deed that shall re-echo round the sphere! Jacinta, you have been most deeply wronged; lead forth a squadron of our girls.

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: You have borne no less.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Oh, Pascuala, for a flag!

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Tie a cloth upon this lance to flourish. We shall have our banner.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Stay not even for that, for now it comes to me: –Every woman her headdress! Wave, banners, wave!

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Name a captain and march!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: We need no captain.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: No? Wave, banners!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: When my courage is up I laugh at the Cid and pale Rodomonte!

div1.stage: Hall in the Castle of the Commander.
Flores, Ortuño, Cimbranos and the Commander enter. Also Frondoso, his hands bound.

lg.l: And by the cord that dangles from his hands
Let him be hung until cut down by death.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: My Lord, you shame your worth.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: String him up on the battlements without further word.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: I had no thought, my Lord, against your life.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: What is this noise outside?

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I hear voices.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Do they threaten your justice, sire?

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: They are breaking down the gates.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: The gate of my castle, the seat of the Commandery?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: The people fill the court.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Within Push, smash, pull down, burn, destroy!

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: I like not their numbers.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Shall these hinds come against me?

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Such passing fury sweeps them that all the outer doors are already beaten in!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Undo this bumpkin. Frondoso, speak to this Alcalde. Warn him of his peril.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Sire, what they do, remember is done in love.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Within Hail, Ferdinand and Isabella, and let the last traitor die!

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Señor, in God’s name you had best conceal your person.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: If they persevere we can hold this room, for the doors are strong. They will turn back as quickly as they came.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: When the people rise and screw their courage to the point, they never stop short of rapine and blood.

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Behind this grating as a barricade we can defend ourselves right stoutly.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Within Free Fuente Ovejuna!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: What a leader for these swine! I will out and fall upon them.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: I marvel at your courage.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Entering Now we meet the tyrant and his minions face to face! Death to the traitor! All for Fuente Ovejuna!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Hold, my people! Stay!

sp.speaker: ALL
sp.p: Wrongs hold not. Vengeance knows no stay!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Tell your wrongs, and on the honor of a knight I’ll requite them, every one.

sp.speaker: ALL
sp.p: Fuente Ovejuna! Long live Ferdinand, our King! Death to traitors and unbelievers!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Will you not hear me? I lift my voice. I am your lord and master.

sp.speaker: ALL
sp.p: No, our lords and masters are the Catholic Kings!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: Stay a little.

sp.speaker: ALL
sp.p: All for Fuente Ovejuna! Die, Fernán Gómez!

div1.stage: Exeunt after breaking through the bars.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Stop here and challenge fortune, no women but an army.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Any that shows herself a woman by mercy, shall swallow the enemy’s blood!

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: We shall spit his body on our pikes.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: As one we stand behind you.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Within Die, traitor though Commander!

sp.speaker: COMMANDER
sp.p: I die! O God, have pity in Thy clemency!

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Within Flores next!

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Have at him, for he landed on me with a thousand whacks.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: I’ll draw his soul out like a tooth!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: They need us there!

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Let them go on! We guard the door.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Within No prayers, no mercy, vermin!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Pascuala, I go with my sword drawn, not sheathed!

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Within Down with Ortuño!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Slash him across the cheek.

div1.stage: Flores enters, fleeing, pursued by Mengo.

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Pity, Mengo! I was not to blame.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: To be a pimp was bad enough, but why the devil lay on me?

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Mengo, give this man to the women. Stay! Stay!

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: ‘Fore God I will! And no punishment could be worse.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Be well avenged!

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Believe me!

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: Run him through!

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: What? Pity, women!

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: His courage well becomes him.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: So he has tears?

sp.speaker: JACINTA
sp.p: Kill him, viper of the vile!

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Down, wretch, and die!

sp.speaker: FLORES
sp.p: Pity, women, pity!

sp.speaker: ORTUÑO
sp.p: I am not the man, I was not guilty!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: In, women, and dye your conquering swords in traitor’s blood. Prove all your courage!

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Die dealing death!

sp.speaker: ALL
sp.p: All for Fuente Ovejuna! Hail, King Ferdinand!

div1.stage: Enter the King Don Ferdinand of Aragon and Queen Isabella of Castile, accompanied by Don Manrique, Master of Santiago.

lg.l: Convenient haste hard following on command,
The victory was gained at little cost,
With slow of slight resistance. Eagerly
We crave a fresh assault to try our prowess.
The Count of Cabra consolidates the front
And fends a counter-stroke, keeping the field.
The troops are well disposed. By our decree
He shall continue in his tents, the line
Reforming, holding the pass. An evil wind
Sweeps up from Portugal, where armed Alfonso
Levies further powers. Cabra shall remain
The head and forefront of our valor here,
Watchful as diligent, that men may see
The danger fly before the sentinel
And peace return with plenty to the land.
By right acclaim in Castile crowned,
Done yet by man from where the sun
To the lands of westering night!

sp.speaker: FLORES

lg.l: O thou great King, my wounds speak,
Where the wretched hinds of the village
Have basely murdered their liege lord
As vassals moving upon slight cause,
Tearing the cross from his breast,

sp.p: After which they cast him from a high window to the ground where he was caught on pikes and sword-points by the women. They bore him in dead and the most revengeful pulled at his beard and hair, defacing every feature, for their fury waxed to such extremity that they sliced off his ears neatly. They beat down his scutcheon with staves and boast outright that they will set the royal arms above the portal where their lord’s should be, full in the square of the village. They sacked the keep as a fallen foe’s, and, exulting, raped his goods and properties. These things I saw, hidden –unhappy was my lot! – and so remained till nightfall, escaping to lay my prayer before you. Justice, Sire, that swift penalty may fall upon these offending churls! Bloodshed this day cries out to God and challenges your rigor!

lg.l: No violence, no cruelty so dire
Escapes the inquest of our royal eye.
I marvel greatly at this villainy,
Wherefore to-day a judge shall be dispatched
To verify the tale, and punishment
Mete out unto the guilty as example.
A captain, too, shall march in his escort
The bolder grown, bolder the chastisement.

div1.stage: The Peasants enter, men and women, bearing the head of Fernán Gómez on a pike.

lg.l: I’ve made a song and, if it’s wrong,
You correct it as it goes along.

l.emph: Just lift them both up to the sky.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: See what you can do, Barrildo.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Silence, then, while I get a rhyme in my head.

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: If you keep your head it will be twice as good.

l.emph: Hail to the King and Queen,
And so they will not blame us.

lg.l: I’m a poet that is one.
You’re the back of the belly.

l.emph: How it hurt to seat me!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: You can take the head off the spear now.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: He might have been hung for his looks. Phew!

div1.stage: Juan Rojo enters with a shield bearing the royal arms.

sp.speaker: REGIDOR
sp.p: Here come the arms!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Let all the people see.

sp.speaker: JUAN ROJO
sp.p: Where shall the arms be set?

sp.speaker: REGIDOR
sp.p: Before the town-hall, here, above the door.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Noble escutcheon, hail!

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: That is a coat of arms!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: I see the light to-day, for the sun begins to shine.

lg.l: King and Queen must needs inquire
Right and wrong as they transpire,

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: That’s a problem too. What shall our story be?

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Let us all agree to die, if it must be, crying Fuente Ovejuna , and may no word of this affair pass beyond that ever.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Besides it is the truth, for what was done, Fuente Ovejuna did it, every man and woman.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Then that shall be our answer?

sp.speaker: ALL
sp.p: Yes!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Now I shall be the Judge and rehearse us all in what we best had do. Mengo, put you to the torture first.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Am I the only candidate?

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: This is but talk, lad.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: All the same let’s get through with it, and quickly.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Who killed the Commander?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Fuente Ovejuna killed him.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: I’ll put you to the torture.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: You will on your life, sir.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Confess, conscienceless hind!

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: I do. What of it?

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Who killed the Commander?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Fuente Ovejuna.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Rack him again! Turn the wheel once more.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: You oblige me.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Reduce him to carrion and let him go.

sp.speaker: CUADRADO
sp.p: What is this meeting?

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Why so grave, Cuadrado?

sp.speaker: CUADRADO
sp.p: The King’s Judge is here.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: All to your homes, and quickly!

sp.speaker: CUADRADO
sp.p: A Captain comes with him also.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Let the devil appear! You know what you are to say?

sp.speaker: CUADRADO
sp.p: They are going through the village prepared to take a deposition of every soul.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Have no fear.–Mengo, who killed the Commander?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Fuente Ovejuna. Ask me who!

div1.stage: Almagro. A room in the Castle.
The Master enters with a Soldier.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: Such news cannot be! To end like this? I have a mind to run you through for your insolence.

sp.speaker: SOLDIER
sp.p: I was sent, Master, without malice.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: Can a mad handful of louts be moved to such fury? I will take five hundred men forthwith and burn the village, leaving no memory of those paths that were so basely trod.

sp.speaker: SOLDIER
sp.p: Master, be not so moved, for they have committed themselves to the King, whose power is not to be gainsaid lightly.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: How can they commit themselves to the King when they are vassals of Calatrava?

sp.speaker: SOLDIER
sp.p: That, Master, you will discuss with the King.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: No, for the land is his and all that it contains. I do obeisance to the Crown, and if they have submitted to the King I will subdue my rage and betake me to his presence as to a father’s. My fault is grievous, in whose palliation I plead my untried years. I hang my head at this mischance of honor, but again to stumble were clear dishonor, yes, and certain death.

div1.stage: The Square of Fuente Ovejuna. Before the Town Hall.

lg.l: Loving, that the beloved should suffer pain
A grinding sorrow fastens on the heart,
Fearing the loved must bear alone the smart
Care weighs the spirit down and hope lies slain.
The firm assurance, watchful to attain,
Doubting falters, and hastens to depart,
Nor is it folly in the brave to start
And tremble, promised boon transformed to bane.
I love my husband dearly. Now I see
Harpies of Vengeance rise before my sight
Unshapely, and my hope breathes a faint breath.
Only his good I seek. Oh, set him free
Ever with me to tremble in the night,
Or take him from me, so you take me, death!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Linger not, Laurencia.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: My dear husband, fly danger, for I am its very heart.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Are you one to reject the homage of a lover?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: My love, I fear for you, and you are my constant care.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Laurencia, I am so happy that surely this moment heaven smiles upon us both.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: You see what has happened to the others, and how this judge proceeds firmly, with all severity? Save yourself before it is too late. Fly and avoid the danger!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: What do you expect in such an hour? Shall I disappear and leave the peril to others, besides absenting myself from your sight? No, counsel me courage, for in danger a man betrays his blood, which is as it should be, come what may. Cries within. I hear cries. They have put a man to the torture unless my ears deceive me. Listen and be still!

div1.stage: The Judge speaks within and Voices are heard in response.

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Old man, I seek only the truth. Speak!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: An old man tortured?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: What barbarity!

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Ease me a little.

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Ease him. Who killed Fernando?

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Fuente Ovejuna.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Good, father! Glory and praise!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Praise God he had the strength!

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Take that boy there. Speak, you pup, for you know! Who was it? He says nothing. Put on the pressure there.

sp.speaker: BOY
sp.p: Judge, Fuente Ovejuna.

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Now by the King, earls, I’ll hang you to the last man! Who killed the Commander?

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: They torture the child and he replies like this?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: There is courage in the village.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Courage and heart.

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Put that woman in the chair. Give her a turn for her good.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: I can’t endure it.

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Peasants, be obstinate and this instrument brings death. So prepare! Who killed the Commander?

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Judge, Fuente Ovejuna.

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Have no mercy.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: I cannot think, my mind is blank!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Frondoso, Pascuala will not tell them.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: The very children hold their peace!

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: They thrive upon it. –More! More!

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: Oh, God in heaven!

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Again, and answer me! Is she deaf?

sp.speaker: PASCUALA
sp.p: I say Fuente Ovejuna.

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Seize that plump lad, half undressed already.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: It must be Mengo! Poor Mengo!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: He can never hold out.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Oh, oh, oh!

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Let him have it.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Oh!

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Prod his memory.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Oh, oh!

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Who slew the Commander, slave?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Oh, oh! I can’t get it out! I’ll tell you –

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Loosen that hand.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: We are lost!

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Let him have it on the back!

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: No, for I’ll give up everything!

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Who killed him?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Judge, Fuente Ovejuna.

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: Have these rogues no nerves that they can laugh at pain? The most likely, too, lie by instinct. I will no more to-day. To the street!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Now God bless Mengo! I was afraid, transfixed, but that lad is a cure for fear.

div1.stage: Barrildo and the Regidor enter with Mengo.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Good, Mengo, good!

sp.speaker: REGIDOR
sp.p: You have delivered us.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Mengo, bravo!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: We cheer you.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Oh, oh! Not much.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Drink, my friend, and eat. Come, come!

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Oh, oh! What have you got?

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Sweet lemon peel.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Oh, oh!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Drink, drink. Take this.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: He does, too.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: He takes it well. Down it goes.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Give him another bite.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Oh, oh!

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Drink this for me.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Swallowed without a smile.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: A sound answer deserves a round drink.

sp.speaker: REGIDOR
sp.p: Another, son?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Oh, oh! Yes, yes!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Drink, for you deserve it.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: He collects for every pang.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Throw a coat around him or he will freeze.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Have you had enough?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: No, three more. Oh, oh!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: He is asking for the wine.

sp.speaker: BARRILDO
sp.p: Yes, let him drink as much as he likes for one good turn begets another. What’s the matter now?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: It leaves a taste in my mouth. Oh, I’m catching cold!

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Another drink will help. Who killed the Commander?

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: Fuente Ovejuna.

div1.stage: Exeunt the Regidor, Mengo and Barrildo.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: He has earned more than they give him. Ah, love, as you are mine confess to me. Who killed the Commander?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Love, Fuente Ovejuna.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: Who?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Don’t you think you can torture me. Fuente Ovejuna.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: It did? How did I get you, then?

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Love, I got you.

div1.stage: Enter the King and Queen, meeting.

sp.speaker: ISABELLA
sp.p: Meeting, Sire, we crown our fortunes gladly.

lg.l: In union lies a more enduring glory.
Passing to Portugal the direct path

sp.speaker: THE KING
sp.p: What news of the war in Castile?

sp.speaker: ISABELLA
sp.p: Peace succeeds and the land lies ready, expecting the plough.

sp.speaker: THE KING
sp.p: Now my eyes light upon a living miracle, the consummation of a queenly peace.

sp.speaker: DON MANRIQUE
sp.p: The Master of Calatrava begs audience, having journeyed to your presence from his seat.

sp.speaker: ISABELLA
sp.p: I have a mind to greet this gentleman.

sp.speaker: DON MANRIQUE
sp.p: Majesty, his years are few, yet they have proved his valor great.

lg.l: I shall lead to smite your foes
Upon my life and oath, or close
My eyes in death! Here I kneel,

sp.speaker: THE KING
sp.p: Rise, Master. Having tendered your allegiance you shall be received royally.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: Every word is balm.

sp.speaker: ISABELLA
sp.p: Few speak as bravely as they fight.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: Esther has returned to earth to wed a Christian Xerxes.

sp.speaker: DON MANRIQUE
sp.p: Sire, the Judge that was dispatched to Fuente Ovejuna has arrived with the process to report to Your Majesty.

sp.speaker: THE KING
sp.p: To the Master These aggressors, being of the Commandery, fall within your province.

sp.speaker: MASTER
sp.p: Sire, I yield to you, else were bloody vengeance taken for the death of the Commander.

sp.speaker: THE KING
sp.p: To the Queen Then the decision rests with me?

sp.speaker: ISABELLA
sp.p: I grant it willingly though the right were mine of God.

sp.speaker: JUDGE
sp.p: I journeyed to Fuente Ovejuna in prosecution of your command probing all with due diligence and care. Having verified the crime, no writ or indictment has issued, inasmuch as with one accord and most singular fortitude, to all my questions as to the murderer the answer was always Fuente Ovejuna. Three hundred were put to torture, to the degree that forced them each to speak, without profit, Sire, of one word other than I have told you. Boys of ten were delivered to the rack, without yielding so much as a whisper, nor could they be moved by flattery or gold. Wherefore, this is my report, the evidence having failed: either you must pardon the village or wipe it out to the last man. They have followed me to your feet that in your own person you may pronounce judgment.

sp.speaker: THE KING
sp.p: If they seek our presence, let them appear before us, every one.

div1.stage: Enter Esteban and Alonso, Alcaldes, Juan Rojo and Cuadrado, Regidors, Laurencia, Frondoso, Mengo and Peasants, both men and women.

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: Are those the King and Queen?

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: The power and majesty of Castile!

sp.speaker: LAURENCIA
sp.p: How beautiful, how wonderful! Saint Antonio, bless them both!

sp.speaker: ISABELLA
sp.p: Are these the people of the village?

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Majesty, Fuente Ovejuna humbly kneels at your feet in allegiance. The mad tyranny and fierce cruelty of the dead Commander, raining insults through the farms, themselves provoked his death. He ravished our homes, forced our daughters, and knew no heart nor mercy.

sp.speaker: FRONDOSO
sp.p: This simple girl, O Queen, who is mine by rite of heaven, and has brought me all happiness, which surely must be matchless, on my wedding-night, as if it had been his very own, he bore off to his keep, and but that she is secure in honor, basely that night he had deflowered her.

sp.speaker: MENGO
sp.p: I know something as to that, with your permission, Queen, because you must be anxious to hear from me, seeing the bloody tanning that I got. I stood up for a girl in the village when the Commander went along the way to her undoing, the scurvy Nero, and then he took it out on me, and there never was a more thorough job at bottom. Three men paid it their attention, good pay all three, since when, if you ask the explanation, I paid more for balm and ointment, with the powder and the myrtle I applied, than I could sell my sheep-cot for.

sp.speaker: ESTEBAN
sp.p: Sire, we yield ourselves to you. You are our King, and in witness of submission we have placed your arms above our doors. Have mercy, Sire, for our excuse is our extremity, which deserves your clemency.

sp.speaker: THE KING
sp.p: As no indictment is set down, although the fault be grave, it shall be pardoned. Since you yield yourselves to me, I further take the town under my protection, for in the Crown henceforth its charter shall abide, until such time as God in His mercy shall vouchsafe you a new Commander.
